---
title: "Code identity"
---


## Two names for every code

Codes get renamed, moved under a different parent and merged into one another
while a project matures. Every export therefore names each code twice:

| Column | What it is | Survives renaming? |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | the path a person reads, e.g. `Belastung/beruflich` | no |
| `codeId` | a stable identifier the plugin assigns once | yes |

## Why it matters for you

Consider an analysis you run in March and again in June. In between, a
colleague renames `Belastung` to `Stress` and moves two subcodes. Grouped by
`code`, the June run quietly reports a different set of codes, nothing
errors, the numbers simply refer to something else. Grouped by `codeId`, the
same codes are still the same codes.

```r
qda_code_counts(frag)                      # by path: readable, fragile
qda_units(frag, value = "codeId")          # by identity: stable
```

Both have their place. Paths belong in figures, because `cX1y2z3a4` means
nothing to a reader. Identities belong in anything that has to line up across
two exports: reliability, before-and-after comparisons, longitudinal work.

A practical compromise is to group by `codeId` and label with the path from the
codebook export, which gives you stability in the computation and readability
in the figure.

## Merged and deleted codes

When two codes are merged, the surviving code keeps its own identity and the
absorbed one is recorded as having moved into it. When a code is deleted, its
identity is not reused. This means the identity of a code you saw in an older
export never silently comes back attached to something else.
